why: The total cost f(x) = 2 * sum |x - center[i]| is convex in x: it falls until the median, then rises. So the suitable points form one contiguous range around the median, and you can binary search its left and right ends separately; prefix sums over sorted centers make each f(x) evaluation O(log n).
hints: Plot f(x) = sum of 2|x - c| as x moves along the line. What shape is it, and where is its minimum?
f is convex with its minimum at the median, so {x : f(x) <= d} is a single interval (or empty). Binary search the leftmost x in [-10^9, median] with f(x) <= d and the rightmost x in [median, 10^9].
Sort centers and build prefix sums; f(x) = 2 * (x*k - sum_left + sum_right - x*(n-k)) where k = number of centers <= x (bisect). Total O(n log n + log(range) * log n).
pitfalls: If f(median) > d the answer is 0; check this before searching.
Do not forget the factor 2 (go and come back).
Only integer x in [-10^9, 10^9] count; clamp the search range.
